yellow: people · pale: records and lists · blue card: the website · green: views · pink: outside · blue arrows: talking to the customer · red: what can go wrong
the customer builds and schedules the move
the sales person confirms, and the move is created
the manager and the crew both see it
rule: a request, not a promise
rule: a deposit is settled once
for the manager and the crew
each move assigned to a crew
rule: nobody on two moves a day
What happens, in order, and why
1 The customer opens the website and builds the move in the calculator: items and weights, both addresses and an available date.
2 The calculator estimates the price from the price list and the distance from maps. The customer submits it.
3 The submitted web quote reaches the sales person as a new request.
4 The sales person calls the customer to go through the move they built, and fixes anything missing or wrong.
5 The sales person checks the schedule, because the website only shows general availability. The customer says yes.
6 The sales person creates the move from the web quote: the price is locked and the date is set.
7 The deposit is charged through the payment provider and recorded in the customer account.
8 The new move appears on the schedule.
9 The manager and the crew both see it.
10 The manager assigns the move to a crew, with its trucks, in the day plan. Move day runs as before.
• A web quote is only a request: nothing is
• The move is created once, from the web quote,
• The deposit is charged when the move is created.
• Cancelling within 7 days of the move keeps the deposit.
• The website shows only general availability per date;
the customer never picks a crew or trucks.
• Only the manager assigns a move to a crew, in the day plan.
• The customer can't be reached: close to the move date
the request is cancelled and the web quote expires.
• More moves than crews on one day: availability is only
general, so the manager re-plans the day.
Weird scenarios: the numbered dots above
6 an open question for the business
Different dates on phone and laptop: which is real?
A stop at a storage unit
Three addresses, not two: what happens to the third?
breaks: a quote has one pickup, one delivery
An employer books for a new hire: who pays?
Yes, but the card is declined
The deposit fails after the yes: is it confirmed?
breaks: the move exists before the deposit
A date the website showed as full
The customer insists by phone: can sales say yes?
open: only the manager knows capacity
How long does the request stay open?
answered: cancelled near the date; quote expires
A truck breaks the day before
Which move loses it, and who tells the customer?
answered: the manager re-plans, sales calls
Whose date changes, and who decides?
open: no rule says which customer moves
A new address after the yes
40 km further: does the locked price hold?
breaks: the move has no way to change
Confirmed, but never met the crew
Nobody is there: how long to wait, and who pays?
part answered: didn't happen, deposit kept
Does the crew start without the customer?
open: who may accept the move?
The truck is full: does the crew unload?
It runs over two days: one move or two?
breaks: a move has one date
Who records it, and does it change what's owed?
Does the sales person still get a share?
answered: share only from money received
Is the sales person's share taken back?
open: can a share be reversed?
